one_month_reasoning: No Micron earnings in the window (FQ1 FY27 report expected mid/late Dec 2026). In-window events: SK hynix Q3 results 28 Oct and Samsung Q3 results ~29 Oct (peer read-through on DRAM/HBM pricing and 2027 HBM contracts), FOMC 27-28 Oct (prediction markets ~17% hike, 83% hold; Kalshi+Polymarket via DefiRate), and late-Oct hyperscaler earnings/capex guides. The FQ4 beat-and-raise (FQ1 guide ~8% above consensus) produced only a +0.9% net move by 2 Oct, so there is a modest post-earnings-drift argument for a small upward tilt, offset by a hawkish Fed path (71% odds of a December hike) and the stock's tendency to sell off on peak-cycle worries. I centre the distribution ~1% above spot (~$1,085) with a ~21% one-month log-sigma (80% annual realized vol / ~3.5, trimmed slightly as event risk is peer-only), i.e. close to symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of FY28 consensus EPS $205.95 x 5.0x (peer memory median ~4.9x) = $1,030 (50%), mid-cycle EPS $145 x 8.0x = $1,160 (25%), and a cycle-aware DCF-lite with a 2029-30 downturn plus accumulated net cash = $855 (25%); blended ~$1,020 for Oct 2027.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Aug-28) consensus EPS $205.95 x 5.0x forward P/E at Oct 2027

At Oct 2027 the market will be pricing a year (FY28) that consensus and Micron see as still tight but closer to the 2028-29 capacity wave, so a peak-cycle multiple at the peer median, not MU's current 6.1x, is used.
Midpoint of BofA bear-case EPS ~$100 (DRAM ASP -30%, NAND -40%, historical-downturn magnitudes) and the FY27/FY28 consensus average ~$191; rounded to $145

Average of MU's forward P/E at the last two cycle peaks (4.5x in 2018, 11x in 2022 per Trefis) is ~7.75x; applied to normalized not peak EPS, and inside the full 11-peer range (4.0x-23.7x), close to Sandisk's 8.0x

inputs_detail.derivation: FQ4 net cash $68.3B + FY27 FCF ~$156B (consensus FY27 EPS $176 x 1.13B shares ~ $199B NI + ~$12B D&A - ~$55B capex) over 1.13B shares; returns via buybacks are value-neutral

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market front-runs the 2028-29 supply wave (ID1, Tongluo, Japan, ID2, Singapore NAND) and/or AI capex digestion; DRAM/NAND price increases stall in 2H27. As in 2018 (-57% at 4.5x forward P/E while EPS still rising) and 2022 (-50%), the stock falls ~50% before earnings peak: ~4x a reduced FY28 EPS of ~$140.

base.story: FY27 delivers ~consensus ($176+) and FY28 still looks tight per management/TrendForce, but the market caps the multiple at peak-cycle ~5x FY28 EPS ~$206; cash builds and capital return rises from Dec 2026. Stock roughly flat with very high path volatility.

bull.story: SCAs (26 deals, ~$150B RPO at floor prices, $32B commitments) persuade investors that this cycle is structurally shallower; supply stays short into 2029-30 (SK hynix chairman view); MU re-rates toward ~8x FY28 EPS of ~$215.

EV/EBITDA 7.0x-43.4x (StockAnalysis figures are trailing EV/EBITDA; forward EV/EBITDA was not available, so the ev_ebitda_fwd field holds trailing values).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 5.0x FY28 EPS sits at the 11-peer median (4.92x) and slightly above the memory-maker cluster; MU currently trades at 6.1x FY27 EPS. The 8.0x through-cycle multiple is applied to normalized (not peak) EPS and sits inside the peer range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No persistent premium assumed. MU's SCAs/RPO and customer deposits are a real difference vs past cycles, but SK hynix and Samsung have similar long-term HBM/DRAM arrangements and still trade ~4.5x, and history (2018 at 4.5x, 2022 at 11x) shows peak multiples compress regardless. A slight uplift vs the 4.5x memory cluster reflects MU's net cash ($68.3B) and US-listing; no sell-side outperformance claim is used.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$600 (-44%) the market would be pricing roughly 6x BofA's historical-downturn bear EPS (~$100) or ~3x FY28 consensus, i.e. an actual price roll-over in DRAM/HBM contracts, SCA renegotiation or an AI-capex cut, not ordinary 80%-vol noise. That is the 2018/2022 peak-reversal path.

key_uncertainties: Timing of the stock's peak relative to the earnings peak: history says the stock turns 2-3 quarters before EPS, and by Oct 2027 the market will be looking at 2028-29 when new fabs (ID1, Japan, ID2, Singapore NAND, NY) add supply.
Whether SCAs with floor pricing (~$150B RPO) make this cycle structurally shallower than 2018/2022.
Durability of hyperscaler AI capex through 2027.
Rate path: prediction markets price a December 2026 hike at ~71%, unusual for a market at record highs.
Capex inflation (FY27 above $50B implied) reducing FCF and signalling industry overbuild.
reasoning: Base-rate anchor: MU's own history shows every prior memory boom ending with a 50-70% drawdown (2014-16 -70%, 2018 -57% from a 4.5x forward P/E while EPS was still rising, 2022 -50% from 11x), and the stock leads earnings by 2-3 quarters. Across 15 macro shocks MU's average drawdown is -34% (2x the S&P), with a median 9-month recovery. The stock is up ~490% in a year, at record 87% gross margins, already 14% below its June high, with 80% realized vol. Against that, the fundamentals right now are the strongest ever: FQ4 revenue $54.2B, FQ1 guide $61.5B/$38.15 (~8% above consensus), management and TrendForce see supply tighter in CY27-28 with prices still rising (more slowly) through 2H27, 26 SCAs with ~$150B RPO at floor prices, $68B net cash. Even BofA's history-calibrated bear case is ~$100 EPS. Valuation at the horizon: the market will price FY28 (~$206 consensus) as at or near peak, so I use the peer memory multiple (~5x) rather than a premium -> ~$1,030, blended with mid-cycle ($1,160) and a cycle-aware DCF ($855) -> ~$1,020. Scenarios: bear $560 (30%, the historic peak-reversal path), base $1,050 (45%), bull $1,700 (25%); mean ~$1,065 and median ~$1,000, slightly below spot. The ladder is a lognormal with ~65% log-vol around a ~$1,000 median, with a slightly thinner far-right tail (peak-cycle earnings cap upside) and a fat left tail matching historic busts. Macro odds: Polymarket put a 2026 US recession at 31% in April (search snapshot later ~23%); a Kalshi 'Recession in 2027' market exists ($599K volume) but its price could not be read. Limitations: X/Twitter was not tried; several Nasdaq history pieces returned 503; peer EV/EBITDA is trailing. Lane share: 12 of 29 sources are in lane; excluding the 12 StockAnalysis peer/company data pages that the comps rule requires, that is 12 of 17 (71%).
